neighbours.label: the closing word-piece of a name whose first piece ends in -y (Lay|ne, Pay|ne, Roy|ce, Hay|nes, Boy|ne, Gay|lord), in any case or use (person, river, brand, username), plus the whole names Lloyd and Boyd; not common words built on -ay/-oy (player, cowboy, joyful, daylight), and weak on names kept as one token (Doyle, Joyce, Floyd)
neighbours.short: name ending after a -y first piece (Lay|ne, Roy|ce)
neighbours.notes: Test sentences written blind by a second author who saw only the label. Feeder found with the resident attribution ranking (play step hit CUDA OOM), so no ablation edge weight.
fire: Detective Marcus Layne walked into the precinct with a cold coffee.
The Boyne flows quietly past the old stone abbey.
Our new neighbor, Mrs. Payne, brought over a lemon cake.
Sir Gaylord tipped his hat and rode off toward the castle.
The engine was built by a firm called Royce & Sons in 1912.
Ask Lloyd whether he finished the quarterly report.
Coach Boyd blew the whistle and the team ran another lap.
Her username was raynor_88 and she posted every morning.
quiet: The detective walked into the precinct with a cold coffee.
The river flows quietly past the old stone abbey.
Our new neighbor, the player, brought over a lemon cake.
The cowboy tipped his hat and rode off toward the castle.
The engine was built by a joyful family firm in 1912.
Ask the employee whether he finished the quarterly report.
The coach blew the whistle and the team ran another lap in daylight.
Her playlist was long and she posted every morning.
